blocks.text: In Materia , his second book following the monograph Epitome , Kyiv-based photographer Vic Bakin sets images against the decay of their own physical support.
By Gaia Squarci. Photographs by Vic Bakin

This work began with two portraits of the same man, made ten years apart. Bakin printed these and other portraits, together with interiors and details hinting at lingering moments, on discontinued photographic paper from the 1960s to the 2000s. Each batch aged differently: faded, spotted with mold or marked by fingerprints.

The paper’s decay seems to mirror the vulnerability of the skin. Fragility, desire, and the relentless pull of time all surface from the same image. As Bakin puts it: “For me, thinking happens through making. I rarely begin with a clear concept. Instead, I make pictures first and then spend months trying to understand what they are telling me.”
The book Materia is published by VOID and available for 60 Euro.
